name: Modern SEO - M2L1 Complete GBP Audit and Optimization
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 2 Three-Step Method](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-2-three-step-method) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
Step 1 of the three-step method, shown on Right Way Driving School (10:03). "If you get the GBP wrong, not very much else matters." Start with a rank map, then audit the [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile). The two most important checks are categories and every field being filled. Findings go into a GBP Review document plus a client questionnaire, and nothing changes until the client approves.

# Key concepts
- **Rank map first.** Normally primary category + city. Here he used "driving school near me" because the client already ranked first for the town term and locals do not search by town.
- **Categories.** Use GMB Everywhere's Category Finder to see competitors' secondary categories; keep only ones that truly describe the business (accepted driver's license training school, rejected test center and car rental).
- **Fill every field:** description, opening date, contact, chat, social links, hours, special hours, all attributes. Most missing answers come from the questionnaire.
- **Links must be correct, not just present** (a Facebook link was flagged for http instead of https).
- **Service areas matter little** (he likes 20; the template says little evidence of ranking impact).
- **More services, no repeats.** Expand from GMB Everywhere, check relevance, then a Claude prompt sorts each service under exactly one best-fit category.
- **Activity checks:** posts (only one, five years old), photos and logo, booking link, review responses, Q&A.

# Steps
1. Run the baseline rank map.
2. Open a blank GBP Review document (Item, Result, Suggestion).
3. Check primary category; research secondary categories in Category Finder.
4. Go section by section through Edit Profile; note every blank or wrong item; list unanswered attributes for the questionnaire.
5. Expand services; remove overlaps; run the Claude sorting prompt.
6. Check posts, photos, booking, reviews, Q&A.
7. Send the GBP Review and questionnaire; change nothing until approved.

# Notable quotes
- "The first and most important is the primary and secondary categories."
- "Remember, we get client permission before making changes to the GBP."

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Record a baseline rank map for [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub) before any GBP change; Kim's visibility tracker is a natural place for it.
- Do a category pass and a categorized, de-duplicated service list per client as a recommendation for Kim and the client to approve.
- Check attributes and links field by field (http links, missing special hours, unanswered attributes, chat).
- GBP photos must follow TAG's rule from Scott's meetings: internal pipe damage or lining work only, never under-sink plumbing.
- Output is a review document or fix list for Kim, never direct edits.

# Caveats and open questions
- Claude's extra suggestions (more categories, "keep 5-10 core services per category visible") came from the AI, not the instructor. Do not treat as course advice.
- "Ahead of 90% of your competition" is an unverified claim.
- GBP Review document, questionnaire and sorting prompt are on the course page, not in the video. LeadSnap and GMB Everywhere may cost money; Kim's approval needed.
